$comment: The processes Dyno may start, for scripts/vm-smoke (docs: scripts/vm-smoke/README.md). Each process is Contents/MacOS/<name> of the installed bundle. parents: who may be its parent (app = the app process; launchd = parent pid 1, allowed only while Launch at login is on). argsPattern keeps the CLI calls of the check itself (dyno-agent status) out of the count. stateFiles name the discovery file the app finds its helper by: the pid in it must be the one live helper, and it is gone after Quit. ready: a command that exits 0 once the helper answers.

loginService.label: net.decryptology.dyno.agent
loginService.manualReason: the app registers its login item with SMAppService, which only the app itself calls; `dyno-agent service install` writes a legacy LaunchAgents plist and bootstraps it with launchctl, a different route that is not what users run. The guest does have an Aqua session, but driving the Settings toggle needs a UI driver (see the GUI VM research), which the headless run does not use: the GUI mode (--gui) drives it through gui.launchAtLogin
loginService.approval: System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions; driven in the GUI mode (--gui).

settleWhy: The supervisor has no fixed spawn wait any more (SPAWN_WAIT and CONNECT_GRACE are gone). The longest respawn timer is the crash-loop backoff capped at 15 s, plus 3 s END_GRACE before the held child is ended on a Retry or hand-over, plus the 2 s polling: 20 s covers one full respawn cycle. A second agent after that is a bug, not a timer.

gui.$comment: For scripts/vm-smoke --gui (README, GUI mode): how a person sees and drives Dyno. windowOwner is the CGWindowList owner; contentRegex a text of the rendered main window; launchAtLogin the AX path to the Settings switch (open: actions until the switch is there; save: the button that applies it), the launchd label, the Login Items rows the app must have (and no other), the text the app shows when macOS needs approval, and the agent's parent after a login start; loginStart the log lines that record how the app decided to start (ADR 0010).

loginStart.restoreWhy: How Dyno should start when loginwindow restores it (the Mac restarted with Dyno running, "Reopen windows") is a product decision not taken yet (handoff dyno-login-blockers.md recommends hidden); until then the GUI run reports what happened.
